title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Keynote Stage. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. The minimal badge hero stays either way.

options.label: Keynote Stage
options.lineage: product launch keynotes: dark stage, one product lit at a time
options.thesis: Every project gets revealed like a launch: one product on stage, one sentence, lights.
materials: the vermilion strap as the only live colour
options.viewport: The badge hero stays quiet and light; scrolling dims the room to black and each project enters as a full-viewport segment with a giant name and its real screens lit.
options.risk: Keynote pomp reads as bravado if the claims inflate; every line must stay factual.

raised.raise: Vermilion is reserved for whatever is currently on stage, never sprinkled as decoration.
Segment counters and indices use one engineered tabular digit form, fixed places, no ornament.
Illustrative screens are stamped as such on stage, the honest slide footnote.

options.label: Release Notes
options.lineage: product changelogs founders read every week
options.thesis: The portfolio as a changelog: each project a shipped release with what changed and why.
options.viewport: Minimal badge hero, then a single scrolling release log with a sticky rail of projects.
options.risk: Familiar: the direction most product-dev sites land on, and there are no real dates to anchor releases.

options.label: Napkin Explainer
options.thesis: The shipped screen with Filip's napkin sketch of the decision drawn right next to it.
options.viewport: Badge hero, then each project as a panel: real screen, marker annotations tracing the decision.
options.case: Holds product clarity (decisions become visible) but founders read it as less senior than a launch.
options.risk: Sloppy sketches read junior; needs real illustration discipline.

options.label: Paper Automata
options.case: Charming mechanism, but founders do not see themselves in paper toys.
options.kept: One accent reserved for the thing currently in motion.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.case: Its interface is numbers, and there are no real metrics to show.
options.kept: One engineered digit form with fixed places.

options.label: Ice Press
options.lineage: expedition newspapers printed on the ice
options.case: Beautiful but archival; wrong era for a startup founder.
options.kept: Leave the honest marks standing: label what is illustrative.

options.label: Neon Circuit
options.case: Glow-on-black is the neon-dev-portfolio cliché founders scroll past.
options.kept: One continuous line of motion rather than scattered effects.

options.label: Highlife Sleeve
options.case: Joyful, but tells founders nothing about shipping software.
options.kept: Colour that owns whole regions instead of timid accents.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer portfolio: intro, project card grid, about, contact, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Badge hero, then a tidy two-column grid of project cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other dev portfolio by design.
